source.title: MEUV: Achieving Fine-Grained Capability Activation in Large Language Models via Mutually Exclusive Unlock Vectors
source.authors: Xin Tong; Zhi Lin; Jingya Wang; Meng Han; Bo Jin

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper evaluates the cited single-direction ablation baseline on new instruction-tuned models and reports harmful-request response rates and benign-task performance. It also tests multi-vector specificity and cross-language transfer.
record.gate_note: Rows record overall harmful-prompt ASR, benign-prompt response rates, USG specificity measurements, the reported component-ablation results, and cross-language results. The paper's RD baseline is described as the cited single-vector method, but it does not state the direction-extraction details. Values mentioned only as hyperparameter or model-selection criteria were not recorded.
record.test_reason: The paper runs the Arditi et al. single-direction ablation (RDablation) on three new instruction-tuned models with English and Chinese harmful and benign prompts. It also reports topic-specificity (USG) and cross-language transfer of its multi-vector method, so it bears on V1, V4 and V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. The authors conclude that refusal can be factored into near-orthogonal topic-aligned unlock vectors, reaching ASR of at least 87% with much better topic specificity than the single-vector baseline and little effect on benign tasks. They say the vectors transfer across languages for two of the three models, which they take to suggest a language-agnostic refusal subspace. The 'little effect on benign tasks' claim rests on a response-rate measure only.
record.recipe_differences: The RD baseline is described as the cited global-direction method and is applied by residual-space ablation at the final residual stream of every transformer block. The paper does not state how RD directions are extracted, so the difference-in-means recipe cannot be verified from this text. MEUV learns topic-specific vectors rather than testing only the original single-direction method.
record.method_sensitivity: Cross-language outcomes vary by model and direction: the authors report a significant decrease for LLaMA-3-8B vectors trained in Chinese and evaluated in English. MEUV specificity also depends on the cross-topic and orthogonality terms; removing either lowers USG.

fits_no_version.finding: MEUV reaches high overall harmful-task unlock rates (0.87-0.94) with benign response rates close to 1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Topic-routed rank-1 ablation vectors can unlock harmful requests at rates similar to a single global direction with little change in benign response rate.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing MEUV's cross-topic penalty or orthogonality term gives similar or higher ASR but lower USG.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Without topic-separation constraints, learned vectors drift toward one generic refusal direction, which gives universal bypass but poor topic isolation.

record.problems: The prompt corpora and reference completions are synthetic, with manual topical verification; the paper gives no uncertainty estimates for the reported table values. Benign capability is assessed on benign samples using a response/refusal-oriented ASR measure rather than a broad capability benchmark. Cross-language values are shown in Figure 6 without exact numbers in the text. The RD direction-extraction details are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 and Table 2 topic-specific ASR columns and their vanilla controls are not separately recorded; the retained overall ASR rows summarize those comparisons. RDaddition is not recorded because its reported harmful-prompt ASR does not test the version's specified addition-induced refusal of harmless requests. Figure 5 heatmap values are not transcribed as separate rows because the text does not give their numeric cell values; the paper's explicit qualitative cross-topic observations are noted in the Table 4 row notes.

untested.parts: Adding the direction to induce refusal on harmless prompts is not tested. The RD direction-extraction recipe is not stated. Capability beyond benign response rate is not measured. The RD ablation here is also applied at every block's residual stream rather than as the original recipe.
The paper does not compare affine, cone, and dominant-direction-plus-others models as competing descriptions of refusal. It tests only whether topic-aligned vectors improve specificity.
Cross-model-variant and base-to-instruct transfer are not tested. Only language transfer of MEUV vectors is tested, not of the RD direction.
Interventions are residual-space hooks, not weight edits.

missing.what: Numeric same-language and transferred ASR/USG values for cross-lingual transfer
RDaddition results on harmful prompts (ASR 0.67-0.95). The paper does not test adding the direction to harmless prompts to induce refusal.
Per-topic ASR columns (drugs, porn, terrorism) for vanilla, RDablation and MEUV
Heatmap cell values showing cross-topic unlocking by single-topic RD vectors

record.verdict_notes: The study's own text calls the RD baseline the most stable white-box unlocking technique, and its RD numbers reproduce high bypass on new models. The data are synthetic, generated with GPT-3.5, with only 3 topics and no uncertainty estimates. The 'ASR' on benign prompts is really a non-refusal rate. The paper evaluates the RD baseline as a comparator rather than as a replication, and does not give the RD extraction details.

versions.untested_parts: The RD ablation baseline is evaluated for harmful-prompt bypass and benign-task response performance. The paper does not evaluate adding a single direction to induce refusals on harmless requests, and it does not specify the direction-extraction recipe in enough detail to verify the difference-in-means procedure.
No weight edit or released-model abliteration procedure is evaluated; interventions use residual-space hooks.
The paper does not test whether jailbreaks suppress the direction or whether training against its ablation improves robustness.
The paper tests topic-aligned multiple unlock vectors and specificity, but does not compare affine, cone, and dominant-direction-plus-others models as competing descriptions of refusal.
No separate harmfulness judgment and refusal-decision representations are tested.
Cross-language transfer is tested. Transfer across model variants or from base to instruct models is not tested.
The study does not compare refusal-training methods or training stages as causes of a removable direction.

rows.operation_detail: USG measures the specificity of topic-wise unlock success across the harmful-topic score matrix.
rows.note: The paper reports lower specificity than MEUV and says single-category RD vectors can unlock other categories.
rows.check: This is the single-direction baseline's specificity (USG), computed from per-topic RD vectors. The state 'partial' is a judgment about MEUV versus RD, not a measure of V4 itself. relationships.reason: Overall ASR rises from 0.08-0.33 to 0.83-0.96 (t1 and t2 RD rows) while benign response stays at 0.98-1.0 (t3 RD rows). The benign test measures non-refusal only, so it does not establish that other abilities are kept.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: RDablation on LLaMA-3-8B, Qwen-2.5-7B and Gemma-2-2B instruct models, English and Chinese harmful prompts; benign prompts still answered
source_check.reason: ASR rises from 0.0783-0.3304 to 0.8261-0.9565 (Tables 1-2), and benign non-refusal stays at 0.9826-1.0 (Table 3). 'Adding induces refusal' and capability retention are untested, which the reason already notes.

relationships.condition: Topic-specific refusal handling in the three instruct models, English and Chinese
relationships.reason: Per-topic RD vectors have low USG (0.37-0.49), meaning each unlocks other topics too. Learned topic-aligned vectors raise USG to 0.74-0.92, but remain below 1 with some residual leakage (t4 rows). Removing the cross-topic or orthogonality terms lowers USG again (t5 USG rows). The evidence is on the paper's own method, with synthetic data and three topics. It suggests refusal splits into partly separable topic components, but it does not compare cone or affine descriptions.
relationships.display_finding: Learned topic-aligned vectors increased USG from 0.37–0.49 to 0.74–0.92 with residual leakage, and removing cross-topic or orthogonality terms reduced selectivity in the synthetic three-topic setting.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Topic-specific refusal handling in the three instruct models, English and Chinese
source_check.reason: Near-orthogonal topic vectors each unlock mainly their own topic (USG 0.74-0.92 vs RD 0.37-0.49, Table 4). Without the constraints they collapse to a generic direction (Table 5), which fits 'dominant direction plus others'. Residual leakage below USG 1 doesn't qualify V4, which does not claim exclusivity. Own method, synthetic data and three topics are untested scope, not limits_scope.

relation.reason: Its own RD-ablation runs bear on V1, and its topic-vector and cross-lingual results bear on V4 and V6.

tranche.reason: The paper runs Arditi et al.'s single-direction ablation itself on three instruct models, in English and Chinese, at the final residual stream of every block. The measure is a refusal-template ASR, close to substring refusal scoring. Extraction details are not given. The main V4 contribution (MEUV) is a different, T2-like method.

source_check.notes: Prompts are synthetic, GPT-3.5-made (test split 460, 115 per label), and ASR is only the absence of a refusal template. The text calls Qwen both 'Qwen-7B' (cites the Qwen2 report) and 'Qwen-2.5-7B-Chat' (tables). RDaddition is used as an unlock method (it raises ASR, unexplained), so V1's 'adding induces refusal' is not tested. The abstract's 'transfer almost unchanged' overstates the body: LLaMA zh-to-en drops significantly.

statements.correction: Chinese (zh-cn) RD-ablation rows: t2-zh-* (Table 2), t3-zh-* (Table 3) and t4-zh-*-rd (Table 4). RD extraction details are not stated.
statements.problem: Nothing wrong for this study. Minor: t4-zh-*-rd rows (per-topic RD ablation on Chinese prompts) also carry language. The text cites Arditi et al. for RD but never says the direction is difference-in-means.

statements.correction: Per-topic RD vectors (one category's data) still unlock other topics: USG 0.37-0.49 (Table 4). The text cites the PORN vector unlocking DRUGS in LLaMA and Qwen. Without the cross-topic loss USG falls to 0.5236/0.4097/0.4029 (LLaMA/Qwen/Gemma, English); without orthogonality it is 0.6725/0.6435/0.7295 (Table 5). Full MEUV topic vectors reach USG 0.7420-0.9189 (Table 4). No cosine with the global direction is reported.
statements.problem: The visible statement gives no numbers for this study (it is truncated). Per-topic RD leakage and constraint-removal results fit 'topic directions overlap', but the cited MEUV rows show the opposite: near-orthogonal topic vectors with high specificity. Overlap here is behavioural (cross-topic unlocking); the paper reports no cosines.
